name: Eccentric wrist extension
summary: Forearm on a table, palm down, lift the weight with the other hand and lower it slowly with the working wrist.
setup: Sit with the forearm resting on a table, wrist over the edge, palm down, a light weight in the hand. Use the other hand to lift the wrist up, then lower it slowly on its own over three to five seconds.
why: The wrist tilts a few centimetres at the edge of a table — below what the pose model resolves. Logged by hand.
contraindications: Sharp pain at the outside of the elbow that lingers after the set.

faults.label: Not assisting back up
faults.tip: Only the lowering is loaded. Use the other hand to return the weight to the top.

faults.label: Dropping the wrist
faults.tip: The slow lowering is the whole point; the way up is assisted.

faults.label: Elbow lifting off the support
faults.tip: The forearm rests on the thigh or table throughout so only the wrist moves.

faults.label: Forearm lifting off the table
faults.cue: Lift it back with the other hand
faults.tip: Only the wrist moves; pin the forearm down.

guide.surface: A table with the wrist over the edge.

points.t: Lowers slowly from up to hanging.
